objects.description: Struct holding function pointers for the allocator suite used by hiredis (malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup, free). It allows configuring custom memory management. Ownership and lifetime are managed by the library; callers typically pass an instance to hiredisSetAllocators to install it. All pointers must be valid and follow C allocation semantics; callocFn should zero-initialize, reallocFn must handle NULL, and freeFn must be compatible with the allocation functions provided.

objects.definition: typedef char *sds;
objects.description: Opaque dynamic string handle used by SDS. It is a typedef to char*, pointing to a heap-allocated, null-terminated character buffer whose header resides immediately before the returned pointer. The header layout varies by length class (sdshdr5/8/16/32/64). Do not free with free(); use sdsfree(). Resize and mutate only via the SDS API.

Packed header layout for very short SDS strings (type 5). Length is stored in the upper 5 bits of the flags byte; no separate alloc field exists. Not instantiated as a distinct header in code paths; present to document on-memory layout when flags indicate SDS_TYPE_5.

Packed header for small SDS strings (type 8). Stores current length and allocation (excluding header and trailing null). Located immediately before the sds pointer and governs capacity and length operations.
Packed header for medium SDS strings (type 16). 16-bit length and allocation fields placed before the sds pointer.
Packed header for large SDS strings (type 32). 32-bit length and allocation, directly preceding the sds pointer.
Packed header for very large SDS strings (type 64). 64-bit length and allocation, located before the sds pointer.

objects.definition: typedef intptr_t ssize_t;
objects.description: Signed size type typedef provided for MSVC builds. Alias to intptr_t, intended to hold byte counts or -1 on error. Only defined when _MSC_VER is set.

Parser work-item describing the current element being parsed in a Redis protocol reply. Tracks type, element count for containers, position within parent, a user-created object pointer, parent linkage, and user privdata. Typically used internally by redisReader and by reply object factories to build hierarchical replies.

Vtable of factory callbacks used by the parser to instantiate user-defined reply objects for each RESP type, plus a destructor. Implementations supply these to redisReaderCreateWithFunctions to control reply representation and memory management.

Streaming RESP/RESP3 protocol parser state. Maintains input buffer, parsing tasks stack, current reply pointer, error state/strings, and user-provided factory callbacks and privdata. Feed data via redisReaderFeed and extract completed replies via redisReaderGetReply. Call redisReaderFree to release resources.

Typedef mapping ssize_t to intptr_t for Microsoft Visual C++ builds on Windows. This provides a signed size type compatible with POSIX ssize_t when compiling with MSVC, where ssize_t is not provided by the standard headers.

objects.definition: typedef ULONG nfds_t;
objects.description: Typedef defining nfds_t as an alias of ULONG on Windows. This mirrors the POSIX nfds_t type used with poll-like APIs to represent the number of file descriptors.

objects.definition:
typedef struct redisReply {
    int type; /* REDIS_REPLY_* */
    long long integer; /* The integer when type is REDIS_REPLY_INTEGER */
    double dval; /* The double when type is REDIS_REPLY_DOUBLE */
    size_t len; /* Length of string */
    char *str; /* Used for REDIS_REPLY_ERROR, REDIS_REPLY_STRING
                  REDIS_REPLY_VERB, REDIS_REPLY_DOUBLE (in additional to dval),
                  and REDIS_REPLY_BIGNUM. */
    char vtype[4]; /* Used for REDIS_REPLY_VERB, contains the null
                      terminated 3 character content type, such as "txt". */
    size_t elements; /* number of elements, for REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY */
    struct redisReply **element; /* elements vector for REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY */
} redisReply;
objects.description: Heap-allocated reply object returned by hiredis command APIs, representing RESP2/RESP3 replies (string, error, integer, double, verb, bignum, array, and push). Fields expose raw data; memory must be freed with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is enabled elsewhere.
Enumeration of underlying transport types used by redisContext and redisOptions to select TCP, Unix domain socket, or already-open file descriptor.

objects.definition:
#ifndef _WIN32
typedef int redisFD;
#define REDIS_INVALID_FD -1
#else
#ifdef _WIN64
typedef unsigned long long redisFD; /* SOCKET = 64-bit UINT_PTR */
#else
typedef unsigned long redisFD;      /* SOCKET = 32-bit UINT_PTR */
#endif
#define REDIS_INVALID_FD ((redisFD)(~0)) /* INVALID_SOCKET */
#endif
objects.description: Platform-dependent file-descriptor type used by hiredis for sockets: int on POSIX, SOCKET-sized unsigned integer on Windows. Use REDIS_INVALID_FD for the invalid value.

Configuration struct used to establish connections. Selects transport (TCP, Unix socket, or existing FD), timeouts, options flags, user data with destructor, and PUSH callbacks. Initialize fields directly or with REDIS_OPTIONS_SET_* macros before calling redisConnectWithOptions.
Function table for pluggable I/O backends (e.g., SSL). Provides hooks for close, freeing private context, async read/write triggers, and low-level read/write operations used by redisContext.

Primary connection handle for hiredis. Manages socket/Fd, buffers, timeouts, connection parameters, optional user data, backend function table, and optional PUSH callback. Create via redisConnect* or redisConnectWithOptions, free with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisCallbackFn)(struct redisAsyncContext*, void*, void*);
objects.description: Function type for reply callbacks invoked when an async Redis command completes. Receives the async context, the reply object, and user privdata.
Node in a singly linked list holding a single reply callback and associated subscription bookkeeping and user privdata.
Container maintaining head/tail pointers for a queue of redisCallback nodes, used for regular replies and pub/sub replies.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisDisconnectCallback)(const struct redisAsyncContext*, int status);
objects.description: Function type invoked when an async connection is terminated (error or user request). Status indicates REDIS_OK or REDIS_ERR.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisConnectCallback)(const struct redisAsyncContext*, int status);
objects.description: Function type invoked when the first write event (connect complete) is received. Status indicates success/error.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisConnectCallbackNC)(struct redisAsyncContext *, int status);
objects.description: Non-const variant of the connect callback signature. Invoked on connect event with mutable context.

objects.definition: typedef void(redisTimerCallback)(void *timer, void *privdata);
objects.description: Function type for timer callbacks scheduled by the event adapter, receiving an opaque timer handle and privdata.

Asynchronous Redis connection context embedding a hiredis redisContext, error state, user data, event-loop hooks, connect/disconnect callbacks, reply queues, address info, subscription bookkeeping, and optional RESP3 push handler.

functions.name: hiredisSetAllocators
functions.description: Configures Hiredis to use the caller-supplied memory allocation functions. Pass a struct of function pointers (malloc/calloc/realloc/strdup/free). Returns the previously configured allocator set, enabling restoration if desired. Use to install custom allocators (e.g., tracking, arenas). Details about default/restored behavior are not specified in this header.
requirements: The pointer ha refers to a hiredisAllocFuncs struct; specific nullability or validation requirements are not stated in this header (unknown).

Each function pointer in ha should be compatible with the respective standard allocator semantics (malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup, free); this is inferred from names and usage but not explicitly specified (inferred).
Callers should assume subsequent hi_malloc/hi_calloc/hi_realloc/hi_strdup/hi_free calls will dispatch through the configured functions (inferred).
The returned hiredisAllocFuncs contains the prior configuration; callers should store it if they plan to restore it later (inferred).

functions.name: hiredisResetAllocators
functions.description: Resets Hiredis’ allocator configuration to its internal default. Intended to undo any custom allocator configuration applied via hiredisSetAllocators. The exact default (e.g., libc allocators) is not documented in this header.
requirements: May be called at any time to restore default allocator configuration; specific ordering or concurrency guarantees are not provided in this header (unknown).

functions.name: hi_malloc
functions.description: Allocates a memory block of the given size using Hiredis’ currently configured malloc function. On non-Windows builds this is an inline wrapper around hiredisAllocFns.mallocFn; on Windows it is provided elsewhere.
requirements: size is a size_t; no explicit range restrictions are specified (unknown).
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL and handle errors appropriately (inferred from allocator behavior).
Behavior with size == 0 is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: hi_calloc
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array using Hiredis’ configured calloc function. On non-Windows builds, an overflow check is performed before dispatching to the configured allocator.
requirements: If SIZE_MAX / size < nmemb, the function returns NULL to avoid size_t overflow; callers must handle a NULL return.
nmemb and size are size_t; no additional range restrictions are specified (unknown).
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL and handle errors appropriately (inferred from allocator behavior).

functions.name: hi_realloc
functions.description: Reallocates the memory block pointed to by ptr to the given size using Hiredis’ configured realloc function. On non-Windows builds this wraps hiredisAllocFns.reallocFn; on Windows it is provided elsewhere.
requirements: ptr should be either NULL or a pointer obtained from hi_malloc/hi_calloc/hi_realloc/hi_strdup under the current allocator configuration; this is inferred from realloc conventions and not explicitly stated (inferred).
size is a size_t; no explicit range restrictions are specified (unknown).

Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL and preserve the original ptr as per realloc semantics of the configured allocator (semantics beyond return value are not specified here; inferred).
Behavior when size == 0 is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: hi_strdup
functions.description: Duplicates a C-string using Hiredis’ configured strdup function, returning a newly-allocated, null-terminated copy. On non-Windows builds this wraps hiredisAllocFns.strdupFn; on Windows it is provided elsewhere.
requirements: str must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string; passing NULL or non-terminated memory is invalid; this is inferred from strdup semantics and not explicitly stated (inferred).
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL and handle errors appropriately (inferred).

functions.name: hi_free
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated via Hiredis’ allocation wrappers (hi_malloc/hi_calloc/hi_realloc/hi_strdup) using the currently configured free function. On non-Windows builds this wraps hiredisAllocFns.freeFn; on Windows it is provided elsewhere.
requirements: ptr should be a pointer previously returned by hi_malloc/hi_calloc/hi_realloc/hi_strdup (and not already freed); this is inferred from free semantics and not explicitly stated (inferred).
Whether passing NULL is permitted is not specified in this header (unknown).
Do not mix different allocator families (e.g., freeing memory not allocated by the configured allocators); inferred requirement (inferred).

functions.name: sdslen
functions.signature: static inline size_t sdslen(const sds s);
functions.description: Return the current length (number of used bytes) of an SDS string. This is O(1) using internal header metadata. Use on SDS-managed strings only, not raw C strings.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL valid SDS pointer returned by SDS APIs (not a raw malloc/c-String).
The SDS must not have been freed.
Thread-safety is unknown; treat s as not concurrently modified.

functions.name: sdsavail
functions.signature: static inline size_t sdsavail(const sds s);
functions.description: Return the number of free bytes available in the allocation of s (capacity minus used length).
requirements: s must be a non-NULL valid SDS pointer returned by SDS APIs.
The SDS must not have been freed.
Do not assume type 5 (sdshdr5) has any free space; it returns 0.

functions.name: sdssetlen
functions.signature: static inline void sdssetlen(sds s, size_t newlen);
functions.description: Set the used length field of an SDS to newlen without reallocating. Low-level helper typically used by other SDS functions or advanced callers.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
newlen must not exceed the total allocated size for s (sdsalloc(s)).
Caller must ensure the buffer has at least newlen bytes of initialized data and that s[newlen] is a valid string terminator if C-string semantics are expected.
Do not use on freed or non-SDS pointers.

functions.name: sdsinclen
functions.signature: static inline void sdsinclen(sds s, size_t inc);
functions.description: Increase the used length field of an SDS by inc. Low-level operation that does not perform bounds checks.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
inc must not cause the length to exceed the total allocation (sdsalloc(s)).
Caller must ensure the underlying buffer content and trailing terminator remain valid after the increment.
Do not use on freed or non-SDS pointers.

functions.name: sdsalloc
functions.signature: static inline size_t sdsalloc(const sds s);
functions.description: Return the total allocation (capacity) associated with s, excluding the header and null terminator for types >5. For type 5 it returns the used length (no separate alloc field).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
Do not call on freed memory or non-SDS pointers.

functions.name: sdssetalloc
functions.signature: static inline void sdssetalloc(sds s, size_t newlen);
functions.description: Set the total allocation field of an SDS header to newlen (low-level). Has no effect for type 5 strings.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
newlen must be consistent with the actual allocated buffer size; caller is responsible for ensuring correctness.
Do not call on freed or non-SDS pointers.

functions.name: sdsnewlen
functions.description: Create a new SDS string copying initlen bytes from init (or creating an uninitialized/zeroed buffer depending on implementation). Returns the new SDS.
requirements: If init is not NULL, it must point to at least initlen bytes readable.
May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return (allocation failure).
Caller is responsible to free with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsnew
functions.description: Create a new SDS string from a null-terminated C string init. Returns the new SDS.
requirements: init must be a valid null-terminated C string (or NULL for empty depending on implementation).
May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return.
Free with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsempty
functions.description: Create and return an empty SDS string (length 0).
requirements: May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return.
Free with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsdup
functions.description: Duplicate an existing SDS string, returning a new independent SDS with the same content.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer (may be empty).
May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return.
Free the result with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsfree
functions.description: Free an SDS string previously allocated by SDS functions. Safe to pass NULL depending on implementation (unknown here).
requirements: s must be either NULL or a pointer returned by SDS allocation APIs (sdsnew*, sdsempty, sdsdup, etc.).
Do not use s after calling sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsgrowzero
functions.description: Resize s to length len, growing as needed and zero-filling any new bytes. Returns possibly reallocated SDS.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
Caller must use the returned pointer (it may change due to reallocation) and check for NULL on allocation failure.
len is the target length (not delta).

functions.name: sdscatlen
functions.signature: sds sdscatlen(sds s, const void *t, size_t len);
functions.description: Append len bytes from buffer t to SDS s. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
t must point to at least len readable bytes (can contain binary data including NULs).
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer (may reallocate) and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscat
functions.description: Append a null-terminated C string t to SDS s. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
t must be a valid null-terminated C string.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscatsds
functions.signature: sds sdscatsds(sds s, const sds t);
functions.description: Append SDS t to SDS s. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s and t must be valid SDS pointers.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscpylen
functions.signature: sds sdscpylen(sds s, const char *t, size_t len);
functions.description: Replace the content of s with the first len bytes of buffer t (binary-safe). Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
t must point to at least len readable bytes.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscpy
functions.description: Replace the content of s with the null-terminated C string t. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
t must be a valid null-terminated C string.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscatvprintf
functions.signature: sds sdscatvprintf(sds s, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Append a formatted string to s using a printf-like format string fmt and a va_list ap. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the provided arguments in ap.
ap must be properly initialized and not reused after modification by this call depending on platform conventions.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscatprintf
functions.description: Append a formatted string to s using printf-like semantics. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching the provided varargs.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdscatfmt
functions.description: Append to s using a specialized, SDS-specific formatting mini-language (implementation-defined). Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
fmt must be a valid format string for this function’s supported specifiers (details not in header; unknown).
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdstrim
functions.description: Trim all characters present in cset from the start and end of s, in place. Returns the modified s (may reallocate depending on implementation).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
cset must be a valid null-terminated C string containing characters to trim.
Caller should use the returned pointer (may reallocate) and check for NULL on failure (unknown if it can fail).

functions.name: sdsrange
functions.signature: int sdsrange(sds s, ssize_t start, ssize_t end);
functions.description: In-place substring operation: keep only the inclusive range [start, end] of s, supporting negative indices (implementation-defined). Returns status integer (semantics not documented here).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
start and end are indices relative to the string; negative indices likely refer to offsets from end (assumed by common SDS behavior; exact semantics not specified here).
Caller should not assume return value semantics beyond success/failure (unknown).

functions.name: sdsupdatelen
functions.description: Recompute and fix the length field of s based on the position of the trailing null byte. Useful after manual buffer modifications.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer with a properly null-terminated buffer.
Buffer must contain no embedded premature null that should be considered content, since this uses C-string length.

functions.name: sdsclear
functions.description: Clear an SDS string to length 0 (content may remain allocated for reuse).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.

functions.name: sdscmp
functions.signature: int sdscmp(const sds s1, const sds s2);
functions.description: Lexicographically compare two SDS strings. Returns an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero similar to strcmp.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid SDS pointers.

functions.name: sdssplitlen
functions.signature: sds *sdssplitlen(const char *s, int len, const char *sep, int seplen, int *count);
functions.description: Split the buffer s (length len) by occurrences of separator sep (length seplen). Returns an array of SDS tokens and sets *count to the number of tokens.
requirements: s must point to at least len readable bytes (may contain binary data).
sep must point to at least seplen readable bytes; seplen should be > 0 (empty separator would be ambiguous; exact behavior unknown).
count must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the token count.
The returned array and contained SDS strings must be freed with sdsfreesplitres().
Caller must check for NULL return on allocation failure.

functions.name: sdsfreesplitres
functions.description: Free the array of SDS tokens and each contained SDS as returned by sdssplitlen or sdssplitargs.
requirements: tokens must be the pointer returned by sdssplitlen/sdssplitargs (or NULL for no-op depending on implementation).
count must match the number of elements in tokens.

functions.name: sdstolower
functions.description: Convert all alphabetic characters in s to lowercase in place.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.

functions.name: sdstoupper
functions.description: Convert all alphabetic characters in s to uppercase in place.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.

functions.name: sdsfromlonglong
functions.description: Create a new SDS string containing the decimal representation of value.
requirements: May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return.
Free the result with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdscatrepr
functions.signature: sds sdscatrepr(sds s, const char *p, size_t len);
functions.description: Append a human-readable, escaped representation of the buffer p (length len) to s (e.g., quoting, escaping control characters). Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
p must point to at least len readable bytes.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdssplitargs
functions.description: Parse a shell-like command line into arguments, handling quotes and escapes (implementation-defined). Returns an array of SDS tokens and stores the count in *argc.
requirements: line must be a valid null-terminated C string.
argc must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the argument count.
Caller must check for NULL return on failure.
Free the result with sdsfreesplitres().

functions.name: sdsmapchars
functions.signature: sds sdsmapchars(sds s, const char *from, const char *to, size_t setlen);
functions.description: Map/translate characters in s: for each i in [0,setlen), replace any occurrence of from[i] with to[i]. Returns s (in place).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
from and to must point to at least setlen readable bytes each.
setlen defines the number of character mappings.

functions.name: sdsjoin
functions.description: Join argc C strings from argv with separator sep into a new SDS. Returns the resulting SDS.
requirements: argv must point to an array of at least argc pointers to null-terminated C strings.
sep must be a valid null-terminated C string (may be empty).
May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return and free with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsjoinsds
functions.signature: sds sdsjoinsds(sds *argv, int argc, const char *sep, size_t seplen);
functions.description: Join argc SDS strings from argv with a separator sep (length seplen) into a new SDS. Binary-safe. Returns the resulting SDS.
requirements: argv must point to an array of at least argc valid SDS pointers.
sep must point to at least seplen readable bytes.
May allocate memory; caller must check for NULL return and free with sdsfree().

functions.name: sdsMakeRoomFor
functions.description: Ensure s has at least addlen bytes of free space available, growing the allocation if needed. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer and check for NULL on failure.
addlen is the required additional free space (0 is allowed).

functions.name: sdsIncrLen
functions.description: Adjust the used length of s by incr (positive to grow into preallocated space, negative to shrink). Intended for low-level/manual buffer writes.
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
Resulting length must remain between 0 and the total allocation; caller must ensure bounds.
Caller should maintain a proper trailing null terminator after modifications.

functions.name: sdsRemoveFreeSpace
functions.description: Resize s to remove extra free space, shrinking the allocation to fit the used length. Returns s (possibly reallocated).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
Caller must assign/use the returned pointer.
May allocate/move memory; check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: sdsAllocSize
functions.description: Return the total size in bytes of the memory allocation associated with s (useful for debugging/alloc accounting).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.

functions.name: sdsAllocPtr
functions.description: Return the raw heap pointer that owns the allocation backing s (the pointer that would be passed to free).
requirements: s must be a valid SDS pointer.
Use for allocator interop; do not modify memory allocator metadata.

functions.name: sds_malloc
functions.description: Allocate size bytes using the allocator configured for SDS and return a pointer to the allocated memory.
requirements: size may be zero or more (behavior for zero size depends on allocator; unknown).
Caller must check for NULL on allocation failure and free with sds_free() or the matching allocator.

functions.name: sds_realloc
functions.description: Reallocate the memory block pointed to by ptr to size bytes using the allocator configured for SDS.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or a pointer previously returned by sds_malloc/sds_realloc (or compatible allocator used by SDS).
Caller must check for NULL on allocation failure.
Freed with sds_free() or matching allocator when no longer needed.

functions.name: sds_free
functions.description: Free a memory block allocated by sds_malloc/sds_realloc using SDS's allocator.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or a pointer previously returned by sds_malloc/sds_realloc (or the matching SDS allocator).
Do not use ptr after freeing.

functions.name: sdsTest
functions.description: Run SDS test suite entry point (only available when compiled with REDIS_TEST). Returns an exit/status code.
requirements: Available only if REDIS_TEST is defined at compile time.
argc and argv must be typical program arguments if used.

functions.name: redisReaderCreateWithFunctions
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new RESP protocol parser (redisReader) that uses the provided callback table to construct reply objects. Typical usage: supply function pointers that create your own reply representations (string, array, integer, etc.), then feed raw RESP bytes via redisReaderFeed and extract completed replies via redisReaderGetReply. The reader maintains an internal buffer and error state (err/errstr).
requirements: fn must be a valid, initialized pointer to a redisReplyObjectFunctions table that remains valid for the lifetime of the redisReader.

The callbacks referenced by fn should be suitable for constructing objects for the reply types you expect to parse (e.g., createString, createArray, createInteger, createNil, createBool, createDouble, freeObject). Leaving required callbacks NULL will result in undefined behavior or errors.
Callers are responsible for eventually releasing the reader with redisReaderFree to avoid memory leaks.
This function returns a pointer to a newly allocated redisReader on success, or NULL on allocation failure (inferred from conventional C allocator patterns).

functions.name: redisReaderFree
functions.description: Frees a redisReader created by redisReaderCreateWithFunctions, releasing its internal buffers and state. After this call, the reader pointer is no longer valid.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to a redisReader previously returned by redisReaderCreateWithFunctions (or compatible constructor).
r must not be used after this call; treat the pointer as invalidated.
Do not call redisReaderFree twice on the same reader (double free).

functions.name: redisReaderFeed
functions.signature: int redisReaderFeed(redisReader *r, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends raw RESP protocol data to the reader’s internal buffer for later parsing. Typically called each time new bytes are read from a socket or file. Returns REDIS_OK on success or REDIS_ERR on failure; on error the reader’s err and errstr are set.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to a redisReader.
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least len bytes; buf may be NULL only if len is 0 (inferred from common API patterns).
len is the number of bytes to feed and may be 0.
The function does not perform I/O; callers must read data from the transport before calling.
Callers should check the return value (REDIS_OK or REDIS_ERR). On REDIS_ERR, consult r->err and r->errstr (via redisReaderGetError macro) for details.
Feeding more data than can be buffered may trigger internal buffer growth constraints (maxbuf) and result in an error (inferred from presence of maxbuf).

functions.name: redisReaderGetReply
functions.description: Parses the internal buffer and, when a complete reply is available, constructs it using the user-provided callbacks and returns it via the out parameter. Intended to be called repeatedly after feeding data. Returns REDIS_OK on success or REDIS_ERR on failure; on error, r->err and r->errstr are set. When no complete reply is yet available, it commonly returns REDIS_OK with *reply set to NULL (library pattern).
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to a redisReader.
reply must be a non-NULL pointer to a void* variable where the resulting reply pointer will be stored.
Callers must check the return value; on REDIS_ERR, consult r->err and r->errstr (via redisReaderGetError macro) for the error.

The lifetime and ownership of the returned reply object depend on the create* callbacks supplied in redisReplyObjectFunctions; callers must manage the object per those semantics, and typically free it with the provided freeObject callback when done.
If the buffer does not yet contain a full reply, callers should expect no object to be produced and continue feeding more data before calling again (inferred from typical incremental parsers).

functions.name: win32_getaddrinfo
functions.signature: int win32_getaddrinfo(const char *node, const char *service, const struct addrinfo *hints, struct addrinfo **res);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX getaddrinfo. Resolves a host/service name into a list of address structures. Use like standard getaddrinfo and free the result with win32_freeaddrinfo. Intended to provide BSD socket API semantics on Windows.
requirements: Winsock must be initialized (call WSAStartup) before using socket APIs on Windows.
res must be a non-null pointer to a struct addrinfo* where the result list pointer will be stored.
hints may be NULL or point to a valid struct addrinfo describing constraints.
node and/or service should follow getaddrinfo semantics (at least one should be non-null/valid per typical API usage).
The returned list must be freed exactly once by calling win32_freeaddrinfo.

functions.name: win32_gai_strerror
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX gai_strerror. Returns a human-readable string describing an EAI_* error code from win32_getaddrinfo or related address resolution calls.
requirements: errcode should be an EAI_* error code obtained from win32_getaddrinfo or related functions.
The returned string pointer is managed by the implementation and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: win32_freeaddrinfo
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX freeaddrinfo. Frees the linked list of addrinfo structures returned by win32_getaddrinfo.
requirements: res must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by win32_getaddrinfo.
Each addrinfo list must be freed exactly once; do not use the pointers after freeing.

functions.name: win32_socket
functions.signature: SOCKET win32_socket(int domain, int type, int protocol);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX socket. Creates an endpoint for communication and returns a SOCKET handle.
requirements: Winsock must be initialized (WSAStartup) before calling.
domain must be a valid address family (e.g., AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_UNIX where supported).
type must be a valid socket type (e.g., SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM).
protocol is typically 0 or a valid protocol number compatible with domain/type.
On success returns a valid SOCKET; caller must close it with win32_close when done.

functions.name: win32_ioctl
functions.signature: int win32_ioctl(SOCKET fd, unsigned long request, unsigned long *argp);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX ioctl on sockets (maps to ioctlsocket). Performs control operations on a socket, such as enabling non-blocking mode.
requirements: fd must be a valid SOCKET returned by win32_socket (and not yet closed).
request must be a valid socket ioctl command (e.g., FIONBIO, FIONREAD).
argp must point to a valid unsigned long if the request requires an in/out argument; it may be NULL only if the specific request allows it (per ioctl semantics).

functions.name: win32_bind
functions.signature: int win32_bind(SOCKET sockfd, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addrlen);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX bind. Assigns a local address to a socket.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid SOCKET created by win32_socket and not yet bound.
addr must point to a valid sockaddr of length addrlen appropriate for the socket's address family.
addrlen must match the actual size of the structure pointed to by addr.
For stream sockets, bind should be called before listen/connect as applicable.

functions.name: win32_connect
functions.signature: int win32_connect(SOCKET sockfd, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addrlen);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX connect. Initiates a connection on a socket to a remote address.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid SOCKET created by win32_socket and not already connected.
addr must point to a valid remote address (sockaddr) appropriate for the socket's address family.
addrlen must match the size of the structure pointed to by addr.
For non-blocking sockets, callers must handle the in-progress connection semantics per standard connect behavior.

functions.name: win32_getsockopt
functions.signature: int win32_getsockopt(SOCKET sockfd, int level, int optname, void *optval, socklen_t *optlen);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX getsockopt. Retrieves an option value for a socket.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid SOCKET.
optval must point to a buffer large enough to receive the option value.
optlen must be non-null; on input it must contain the size of the buffer pointed to by optval, and on output it is set to the actual size of the value returned.
level and optname must specify a valid socket option for the given socket (e.g., SOL_SOCKET/SO_KEEPALIVE, IPPROTO_TCP/TCP_NODELAY).

functions.name: win32_setsockopt
functions.signature: int win32_setsockopt(SOCKET sockfd, int level, int optname, const void *optval, socklen_t optlen);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX setsockopt. Sets an option value on a socket.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid SOCKET.
optval must point to a buffer containing the option value expected by the specified level/optname (unless the specific option allows NULL).
optlen must be the size in bytes of the data pointed to by optval.
level and optname must correspond to a valid, supported option for the socket.

functions.name: win32_close
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX close (maps to closesocket). Closes a SOCKET handle.
requirements: fd must be a valid SOCKET obtained from win32_socket (and not already closed).
After a successful close, the SOCKET must not be used again.
Callers should handle the return value and any error reporting consistent with socket close semantics on Windows.

functions.name: win32_recv
functions.signature: ssize_t win32_recv(SOCKET sockfd, void *buf, size_t len, int flags);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX recv. Receives data from a connected socket into a buffer.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid, connected SOCKET.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len specifies the maximum number of bytes to receive and should be > 0 for actual data receipt.
flags should be a combination of supported MSG_* flags for recv on the platform.
Callers must handle the return value semantics: number of bytes received on success, 0 for orderly shutdown, and a negative value on error (per ssize_t semantics).

functions.name: win32_send
functions.signature: ssize_t win32_send(SOCKET sockfd, const void *buf, size_t len, int flags);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX send. Sends data on a connected socket from the provided buffer.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid, connected SOCKET.
buf must point to a readable buffer containing at least len bytes to send.
len is the number of bytes to attempt to send; it may be 0 for a no-op.
flags should be a combination of supported MSG_* flags for send on the platform.
Callers must check the return value: number of bytes sent on success; a negative value indicates an error; short sends are possible and must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: win32_poll
functions.signature: int win32_poll(struct pollfd *fds, nfds_t nfds, int timeout);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX poll (maps to WSAPoll). Monitors multiple file descriptors (sockets) for readiness events.
requirements: fds must point to an array of at least nfds struct pollfd entries.
nfds specifies the number of elements in the fds array.
timeout is specified in milliseconds; a negative value (typically -1) indicates an infinite wait; 0 returns immediately.
Only SOCKET descriptors are supported on Windows; each pollfd.fd must be a valid SOCKET.

functions.name: win32_redisKeepAlive
functions.description: Enables and configures TCP keep-alive on a Windows socket for Redis compatibility. Likely sets keep-alive parameters such as idle/interval using Windows-specific options.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid TCP SOCKET.
interval_ms should be a positive integer representing the desired keep-alive interval in milliseconds.
Socket must be created and (typically) connected before enabling keep-alive.
Caller should check the return value to ensure the operation succeeded.
Exact semantics and supported ranges for interval_ms are not specified in this header and may depend on the underlying Windows TCP stack.

functions.name: redisReaderCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RESP protocol reader instance used to parse Redis replies from a byte stream.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller must eventually free the reader using the corresponding reader free function from the hiredis reader API (not shown in this header).
Returned pointer must be checked for NULL to detect allocation failure.

functions.name: freeReplyObject
functions.description: Frees a reply object previously returned by hiredis (e.g., by redisCommand/redisGetReply). Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: The reply argument must be a pointer obtained from hiredis reply-producing APIs (e.g., redisCommand, redisGetReply).
Do not use the reply after this function returns.
It is valid to pass NULL.

functions.name: redisvFormatCommand
functions.signature: int redisvFormatCommand(char **target, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command using a printf-like format string and a va_list, allocating a protocol-compliant command buffer and returning its length.
requirements: target must be a non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success *target is set to a heap-allocated buffer.
Caller must free the returned buffer with redisFreeCommand.
format must be a non-NULL format string understood by hiredis’ command formatter.
ap must be a valid initialized va_list matching format.
Return value should be checked; a negative value indicates an error and target is not set.

functions.name: redisFormatCommand
functions.description: Formats a Redis command using a printf-like format string and variadic arguments, allocating a protocol-compliant command buffer and returning its length.
requirements: target must be a non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success *target is set to a heap-allocated buffer.
Caller must free the returned buffer with redisFreeCommand.
format must be a non-NULL format string understood by hiredis’ command formatter.
Return value should be checked; a negative value indicates an error and target is not set.

functions.name: redisFormatCommandArgv
functions.signature: long long redisFormatCommandArgv(char **target, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from an argument vector (argc/argv), producing a protocol-compliant buffer and returning its length.
requirements: target must be a non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success *target is set to a heap-allocated buffer.
Caller must free the returned buffer with redisFreeCommand.
argc must be >= 0.
argv must be non-NULL when argc > 0 and contain argc pointers to argument data.
If argvlen is non-NULL, it must point to an array of argc lengths; if NULL, arguments are treated as null-terminated strings.
Return value must be checked; a negative value indicates an error and target is not set.

functions.name: redisFormatSdsCommandArgv
functions.signature: long long redisFormatSdsCommandArgv(sds *target, int argc, const char ** argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from an argument vector into an sds string, returning the length of the resulting protocol-compliant buffer.
requirements: target must be a non-NULL pointer to an sds; on success *target receives a newly allocated sds.
Caller must free the returned sds with redisFreeSdsCommand.
argc must be >= 0.
argv must be non-NULL when argc > 0 and contain argc pointers to argument data.
If argvlen is non-NULL, it must point to an array of argc lengths; if NULL, arguments are treated as null-terminated strings.
Return value must be checked; a negative value indicates an error and target is not set.

functions.name: redisFreeCommand
functions.description: Frees a command buffer previously allocated by redisFormatCommand/redisvFormatCommand/redisFormatCommandArgv.
requirements: cmd must be a pointer previously returned by a hiredis command formatting function.
Do not use cmd after freeing.
It is safe to pass NULL.

functions.name: redisFreeSdsCommand
functions.description: Frees an sds command buffer previously allocated by redisFormatSdsCommandArgv.
requirements: cmd must be an sds previously returned by redisFormatSdsCommandArgv.
Do not use cmd after freeing.
It is safe to pass NULL.

functions.name: redisConnectWithOptions
functions.description: Creates a new Redis connection using the provided redisOptions (TCP, UNIX socket, or an existing file descriptor) and returns a context.
requirements: options must be a non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized redisOptions structure with a valid type and corresponding endpoint fields.
If using TCP, options->endpoint.tcp.ip must be non-NULL and port must be set; optional source_addr may be set.
If using UNIX sockets, options->endpoint.unix_socket must be non-NULL.
If using an existing FD, options->endpoint.fd must refer to a valid open socket.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnect
functions.description: Creates a blocking TCP connection to the specified Redis server and returns a context.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL address string.
port must be a valid TCP port (>0).
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectWithTimeout
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectWithTimeout(const char *ip, int port, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Creates a blocking TCP connection to the specified Redis server with a connect timeout and returns a context.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL address string.
port must be a valid TCP port (>0).
tv specifies the connect timeout; its fields should represent a non-negative interval.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectNonBlock
functions.description: Creates a non-blocking TCP connection to the specified Redis server and returns a context.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL address string.
port must be a valid TCP port (>0).
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop to complete the connection and I/O.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectBindNonBlock
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectBindNonBlock(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Creates a non-blocking TCP connection binding the local side to source_addr before connecting to ip:port.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL address string.
port must be a valid TCP port (>0).
source_addr must be a non-NULL local address string.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop to complete the connection and I/O.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectBindNonBlockWithReuse
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectBindNonBlockWithReuse(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Creates a non-blocking TCP connection binding to source_addr with SO_REUSEADDR semantics before connecting to ip:port.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL address string.
port must be a valid TCP port (>0).
source_addr must be a non-NULL local address string.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop to complete the connection and I/O.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectUnix
functions.description: Creates a blocking connection to a Redis server via a UNIX domain socket path and returns a context.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectUnixWithTimeout
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectUnixWithTimeout(const char *path, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Creates a blocking UNIX domain socket connection with a connect timeout and returns a context.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
tv specifies the connect timeout; its fields should represent a non-negative interval.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectUnixNonBlock
functions.description: Creates a non-blocking UNIX domain socket connection to a Redis server and returns a context.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop to complete the connection and I/O.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisConnectFd
functions.description: Wraps an already-open socket file descriptor in a hiredis context for use with the API.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open socket file descriptor suitable for a Redis connection.
Ownership of fd remains with the context until freed or extracted via redisFreeKeepFd.
Check the returned pointer; on error, context->err/errstr will be set.
Caller must free the context with redisFree (or redisFreeKeepFd) when done.

functions.name: redisReconnect
functions.description: Reconnects the given context using the previously saved connect options, reusing host/path, timeout, bind address, and flags.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL pointer to a redisContext previously created by a connect function.
Only call when the context is disconnected or in an error state that requires reconnection.
Return value must be checked: REDIS_OK indicates success; REDIS_ERR indicates failure.

functions.name: redisSetPushCallback
functions.description: Sets the RESP3 PUSH message callback on the context, enabling asynchronous server-initiated messages to be handled by fn. Returns a pointer (semantics not documented here; likely the previous callback).
requirements: c must be a non-NULL, valid redisContext.
fn may be NULL to clear the callback.
Caller should ensure the callback is safe to call from hiredis’ internal I/O paths.

functions.name: redisSetTimeout
functions.signature: int redisSetTimeout(redisContext *c, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Sets the command timeout on the context; affects blocking operations such as reads and writes after this call.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL, valid redisContext.
tv must represent a non-negative interval.
Return value should be checked to confirm the timeout was applied.

functions.name: redisEnableKeepAlive
functions.description: Enables TCP keepalive on the connection using a default interval.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL, connected TCP-based redisContext.
Return value should be checked to verify keepalive was enabled.

functions.name: redisEnableKeepAliveWithInterval
functions.description: Enables TCP keepalive on the connection using the specified interval (seconds).
requirements: c must be a non-NULL, connected TCP-based redisContext.
interval should be a positive number of seconds.
Return value should be checked to verify keepalive was enabled.

functions.name: redisSetTcpUserTimeout
functions.description: Sets the TCP_USER_TIMEOUT socket option (where supported) on the connection to the specified timeout in milliseconds.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL, connected TCP-based redisContext.
timeout is an unsigned millisecond value; must be within the platform’s valid range.
Return value should be checked; failure may indicate unsupported option or other socket errors.

functions.name: redisFree
functions.description: Closes the connection (if open), frees internal resources, and deallocates the redisContext.
requirements: c may be NULL (no effect).
After this call the context pointer must not be used.
If the context holds user privdata with a destructor, it may be invoked during free.

functions.name: redisFreeKeepFd
functions.description: Frees the redisContext but keeps and returns the underlying socket file descriptor to the caller.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext created by a connect function.
Caller becomes responsible for closing the returned file descriptor.
Context must not be used after the call.

functions.name: redisBufferRead
functions.description: Attempts to read pending data from the socket into the context’s read buffer and parse replies.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext with an active connection (typically non-blocking I/O integration).
Return value should be checked; a negative value or context->err indicates an error.

functions.name: redisBufferWrite
functions.description: Attempts to flush the context’s output buffer to the socket. In non-blocking use, call until done is non-zero.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext with an active connection.
done may be NULL; if non-NULL, it points to an int set to non-zero when the output buffer has been fully written.
Return value should be checked; a negative value or context->err indicates an error.

functions.name: redisGetReply
functions.description: Retrieves the next available reply. In blocking mode, flushes output and reads until a reply is available; in non-blocking mode, returns unconsumed replies if available.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
reply must be a non-NULL pointer to a void*; on success, *reply receives a heap-allocated reply object that must be freed with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is enabled.
Caller must handle return codes and context->err to detect errors.

functions.name: redisGetReplyFromReader
functions.description: Parses and returns a reply from the context’s reader without performing socket I/O; returns any reply already buffered.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
reply must be a non-NULL pointer to a void*; on success, *reply receives a heap-allocated reply object that must be freed with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is enabled.
Use after feeding data via redisBufferRead or custom reader feeds.

functions.name: redisAppendFormattedCommand
functions.signature: int redisAppendFormattedCommand(redisContext *c, const char *cmd, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends a pre-formatted Redis protocol command to the context’s output buffer for later sending (pipelining).
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
cmd must point to a buffer containing a complete, protocol-compliant command of length len.
len must be the exact size of cmd; must be > 0 for non-empty commands.
Return value should be checked; a negative value or context->err indicates an error.

functions.name: redisvAppendCommand
functions.signature: int redisvAppendCommand(redisContext *c, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a command using a printf-like format and appends it to the context’s output buffer (used for pipelining).
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
format must be a non-NULL format string understood by hiredis.
ap must be a valid initialized va_list matching format.
Return value should be checked; a negative value or context->err indicates an error.

functions.name: redisAppendCommand
functions.description: Formats a command using a printf-like format and appends it to the context’s output buffer (used for pipelining).
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
format must be a non-NULL format string understood by hiredis.
Return value should be checked; a negative value or context->err indicates an error.

functions.name: redisAppendCommandArgv
functions.signature: int redisAppendCommandArgv(redisContext *c, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a command from an argument vector and appends it to the context’s output buffer (used for pipelining).
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
argc must be >= 0.
argv must be non-NULL when argc > 0 and contain argc pointers to argument data.
If argvlen is non-NULL, it must point to an array of argc lengths; if NULL, arguments are treated as null-terminated strings.
Return value should be checked; a negative value or context->err indicates an error.

functions.name: redisvCommand
functions.description: Issues a command. In blocking mode, behaves like append + get reply and returns a reply object; in non-blocking mode, behaves like append-only and returns NULL.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
format must be a non-NULL format string understood by hiredis; ap must match format.
In blocking mode, the returned reply must be freed with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is enabled.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect errors or non-blocking behavior.

functions.name: redisCommand
functions.description: Issues a command. In blocking mode, formats, sends, and waits for the reply, returning a reply object; in non-blocking mode, formats and appends only, returning NULL.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
format must be a non-NULL format string understood by hiredis.
In blocking mode, the returned reply must be freed with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is enabled.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect errors or non-blocking behavior.

functions.name: redisCommandArgv
functions.signature: void *redisCommandArgv(redisContext *c, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Issues a command built from an argument vector. In blocking mode, sends and waits for the reply, returning a reply object; in non-blocking mode, appends only and returns NULL.
requirements: c must be a non-NULL redisContext.
argc must be >= 0.
argv must be non-NULL when argc > 0 and contain argc pointers to argument data.
If argvlen is non-NULL, it must point to an array of argc lengths; if NULL, arguments are treated as null-terminated strings.
In blocking mode, the returned reply must be freed with freeReplyObject unless auto-free is enabled.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect errors or non-blocking behavior.

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectWithOptions
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous Redis connection using a redisOptions structure. The options specify connection parameters (e.g., TCP, UNIX socket, timeouts, authentication) as defined by hiredis. Returns a newly allocated redisAsyncContext on success, or NULL/err set on failure. Use this when you need fine-grained configuration beyond simple host/port or path.
requirements: options must point to a valid, initialized redisOptions structure as defined by hiredis.h.
The returned redisAsyncContext must be integrated with an event loop by setting ac->ev hooks or using a helper adapter before I/O can proceed.
Callers must set connect/disconnect callbacks as needed before starting the event loop to be notified of connection state.
On success, the caller is responsible for eventually calling redisAsyncFree(ac).
Do not use the context from multiple threads unless explicitly documented by hiredis (thread-safety is unknown).

functions.name: redisAsyncConnect
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous Redis TCP connection to the specified server address and port. Returns a newly allocated redisAsyncContext for use with an event loop.
requirements: ip must be a valid, null-terminated address string resolvable/acceptable by connect(2) (e.g., an IPv4/IPv6 textual address).
port must be a valid TCP port number (typically 0–65535).
The returned context must be attached to an event loop via ac->ev hooks or an adapter before I/O.
Set connection/disconnection callbacks if the application needs notifications.
Caller must eventually free the context with redisAsyncFree(ac).

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectBind
functions.signature: redisAsyncContext *redisAsyncConnectBind(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous TCP connection to ip:port, binding the local socket to source_addr before connecting. Useful for selecting the outbound interface/local address.
requirements: ip must be a valid, null-terminated remote address string.
port must be a valid TCP port number (typically 0–65535).
source_addr must be a valid, null-terminated local address string accepted by bind(2) for the chosen address family.
The returned context must be integrated with an event loop via ac->ev hooks before use.
Caller must eventually free the context with redisAsyncFree(ac).

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectBindWithReuse
functions.signature: redisAsyncContext *redisAsyncConnectBindWithReuse(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Like redisAsyncConnectBind but binds the local socket with address reuse enabled (e.g., enabling SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT as implemented by hiredis). Returns a new asynchronous context.
requirements: ip must be a valid, null-terminated remote address string.
port must be a valid TCP port number (typically 0–65535).
source_addr must be a valid, null-terminated local address string acceptable to bind(2).
The returned context must be attached to an event loop via ac->ev hooks before use.
Caller must eventually free the context with redisAsyncFree(ac).
Exact socket options used for reuse are implementation-defined; specifics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectUnix
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous Redis connection over a UNIX domain socket at the given filesystem path. Returns a redisAsyncContext for use with an event loop.
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated filesystem path to a UNIX domain socket.
The returned context must be integrated with an event loop via ac->ev hooks or an adapter before I/O.
Caller must eventually free the context with redisAsyncFree(ac).

functions.name: redisAsyncSetConnectCallback
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when the connection is established (first write event). Use to be notified of connection success or failure. Returns a status code (exact values are not specified here).
requirements: ac must be a valid pointer to an initialized redisAsyncContext.
fn must be a valid function pointer; passing NULL is not documented as allowed.
Should be set before running the event loop or initiating I/O so the event can be delivered.
Callback signature: void (*fn)(const redisAsyncContext*, int status); status values are library-defined (unknown here).

functions.name: redisAsyncSetConnectCallbackNC
functions.description: Register a non-const-context connect callback variant invoked on initial connect readiness. Returns a status code (unspecified here).
requirements: ac must be a valid pointer to an initialized redisAsyncContext.
fn must be a valid function pointer; NULL allowance is unspecified.
Should be set before running the event loop or initiating I/O.
Callback signature: void (*fn)(redisAsyncContext*, int status).

functions.name: redisAsyncSetDisconnectCallback
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when the connection is terminated either due to error or user request. The callback receives a status indicating REDIS_OK or REDIS_ERR as implemented by hiredis.
requirements: ac must be a valid pointer to an initialized redisAsyncContext.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to generate a single bytes buffer that the harness will split to feed
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR occurrences and unsigned int parameters. The target stubs
# heavily rely on C null-terminated strings (C-strings). Therefore, we will
# generate a concatenation of multiple C-strings separated by NUL (\x00), so
# each FUZZ_PARAM_STR can consume a valid, bounded string. We will also embed
# some binary-safe sections and variety to exercise different code paths.
#
# Design:
# - Produce a sequence of C-strings tailored for the stubs:
#   * General text tokens (words, sentences, JSON-like, shell-like) for sdssplitargs/sdsjoin
#   * Small/medium/large strings for sdsnew/sdscat/sdscpy/sdstrim
#   * Edge-case strings: empty, whitespace-only, special trim sets, separators
#   * Redis-like keys/values and command verbs for redisFormatCommand and async API
#   * Paths and IPs/ports-like tokens for async connect variants
# - Interleave a few numeric seeds encoded as 4-byte little-endian to be read
#   as unsigned ints by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) calls. The harness models often
#   read such integers interspersed with strings; many fuzzers feed both from
#   the same buffer. Here we convert numbers into decimal strings and also pack
#   raw bytes preceded by a marker string to keep overall buffer as C-strings.
#
# The buffer will be a sequence of null-terminated strings; any binary segments
# we embed will be base64 or hex-like to remain C-string friendly. Size limited
# to <= 4096 bytes.

ALPHABET = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '


def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _make_ip(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # IPv4
        return ".".join(str(r.randrange(0, 256)) for _ in range(4))
    else:
        # IPv6 (compressed/simple forms)
        hextets = [format(r.randrange(0, 65536), 'x') for _ in range(r.randrange(3, 8))]
        s = ":".join(hextets)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            s = s + "::"
        return s


def _make_unix_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = ["/tmp", "var", "run", "redis", ''.join(r.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(r.randrange(3, 10)))]
    # ensure starts with slash for a plausible path
    p = "/" + "/".join(parts[:r.randrange(2, len(parts)+1)])
    if not p.endswith(".sock") and r.random() < 0.6:
        p += ".sock"
    return p


def _rand_text(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, printable: bool = True) -> str:
    L = r.randrange(min_len, max_len + 1)
    alphabet = PRINTABLE if printable else ALPHABET
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(L))


def _shell_like_line(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build something sdssplitargs can parse: quotes, escapes, spaces
    args = []
    n = r.randrange(1, 8)
    for i in range(n):
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.2:
            args.append('')
        elif t < 0.45:
            args.append(_rand_text(r, 1, 8))
        elif t < 0.7:
            # quoted with spaces
            args.append('"' + _rand_text(r, 1, 10).replace('"', '\\"') + '"')
        else:
            # escaped spaces and backslashes
            raw = _rand_text(r, 3, 10)
            raw = raw.replace(' ', '\\ ').replace('\\', '\\\\')
            args.append(raw)
    return ' '.join(args)


def _trim_set(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common trim sets: whitespace, punctuation, specific chars
    candidates = [
        " \t\r\n",
        "0",
        "xX",
        ",.;:",
        "[]{}()",
        "\"'",
        string.ascii_lowercase,
        string.ascii_uppercase,
        string.digits,
    ]
    c = _rand_choice(r, candidates)
    # limit size to 32-64
    if len(c) > 64:
        c = c[:64]
    return c


def _sep(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(r, [",", "|", ":", " ", "::", "\t", "-", "/", "\n"])


def _redis_key(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prefixes = ["user:", "sess:", "cache:", "cfg:", "tmp:", "k:"]
    return _rand_choice(r, prefixes) + _rand_text(r, 1, 16)


def _redis_val(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # value with mix of printable and some escapes
    v = _rand_text(r, 0, 64)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        v += "\\n" + _rand_text(r, 0, 16)
    return v


def _build_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # For sdsnew (NULL or string): include empty and normal strings
    out += [
        "",  # empty
        _rand_text(r, 1, 32),
        _rand_text(r, 50, 200),
    ]

    # For sdscat/sdscpy: small to mid strings
    for _ in range(5):
        out.append(_rand_text(r, 0, 64))

    # For sdstrim cset
    out.append(_trim_set(r))

    # For sdssplitargs: shell-like line
    for _ in range(3):
        out.append(_shell_like_line(r))

    # For sdsjoin: several items and separators
    for _ in range(2):
        out.append(_sep(r))
        for __ in range(r.randrange(2, 6)):
            out.append(_rand_text(r, 0, 20))

    # For hi_strdup: typical C-string content
    out += [
        "hello", "world", "foo\0bar".split("\0")[0],  # ensure pre-NUL content only
        _rand_text(r, 1, 32),
    ]

    # For redisFormatCommand branches
    # PING
    out.append("PING")
    # SET %b %b: keys and values (but FUZZ_PARAM_STR supplies data)
    out.append(_redis_key(r))
    out.append(_redis_val(r))
    # INCRBY key
    out.append(_redis_key(r))

    # For redisAppendCommand: keys and values small
    out.append(_rand_text(r, 0, 32))
    out.append(_rand_text(r, 0, 32))

    # For async connect variants: IPs, ports as strings, and source addresses
    for _ in range(3):
        out.append(_make_ip(r))
    out.append(_make_unix_path(r))

    # For async argv: verbs and args
    out += ["PING", "ECHO", "GET", "SET"]
    for _ in range(6):
        out.append(_rand_text(r, 0, 30))

    # Additional edge cases: whitespace-only, large-ish (capped by fuzzer to 1024)
    out.append(" " * r.randrange(0, 32))
    out.append("\t\n\r")

    # Ensure diversity but keep total count moderate
    r.shuffle(out)

    # cap total size after NUL-joining later
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    parts = _build_strings(r)

    # Also inject some decimal integers that will be used by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    # These are embedded as strings, so both string and integer consumers get plausible data.
    ints = [
        str(r.randrange(0, 2**32 - 1)),
        str(r.randrange(0, 65536)),
        "0",
        "1",
        str(r.randrange(0, 100000)),
    ]
    parts += ints

    # Add some separators and special trim sets near the end
    parts += ["\"'\t ", "\n", ",;:\t"]

    # Build the final buffer as NUL-terminated strings sequence. Some fuzzers
    # read until NUL for C-strings and also consume raw bytes; this format fits
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR expectations and provides many fields.
    blob = bytearray()
    for s in parts:
        # Ensure s is str
        if not isinstance(s, str):
            s = str(s)
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        # Limit individual string length to keep total under 4096
        if len(b) > 1024:
            b = b[:1024]
        blob += b + b"\x00"
        if len(blob) > 3800:
            break

    # Make sure we end with an extra NUL to safely terminate last field
    if not blob or blob[-1] != 0:
        blob += b"\x00"

    # Final size cap
    return bytes(blob[:4096])

import random
import struct
import itertools

# We generate valid buffers for the "binary data" type consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# across the provided stubs. The stubs cap strings at certain sizes (mostly 1024),
# and expect arbitrary bytes (including NULs). We craft RESP snippets for
# redisReaderFeed and interesting SDS payloads for other APIs. We keep size <= 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Some helpful byte sequences
PRINTABLE = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-.:/,\n\r\t "
CONTROL_BYTES = bytes(range(0x00, 0x20)) + b"\x7f"
UNICODE_UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "προβατο".encode("utf-8"),
    "表情🙂数据".encode("utf-8"),
    "emoji🚀pile💥".encode("utf-8"),
]

# RESP helpers: craft small valid RESP replies that hiredis reader can parse

def resp_simple_string(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"+" + s + b"\r\n"

def resp_error(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"-" + s + b"\r\n"

def resp_integer(i: int) -> bytes:
    return b":" + str(i).encode() + b"\r\n"

def resp_bulk(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"$" + str(len(b)).encode() + b"\r\n" + b + b"\r\n"

def resp_null_bulk() -> bytes:
    return b"$-1\r\n"

def resp_array(items: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    return b"*" + str(len(items)).encode() + b"\r\n" + b"".join(items)

def resp_push(items: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # RESP3 push type; still valid for reader exercising
    return b">" + str(len(items)).encode() + b"\r\n" + b"".join(items)

# SDS-oriented interesting fragments

def sds_interesting_chunks(r: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    pieces = []
    # Binary with NULs
    pieces.append(b"A\x00B\x00C\x00")
    # Repeated separators for sdssplitlen
    sep = r.choice([b",", b"::", b"|", b"\t", b" "]) * r.randint(1, 3)
    parts = [b"key", b"value", b"another", b"piece"]
    pieces.append(sep.join(parts))
    # Control bytes and printable mix
    pieces.append(bytes(r.sample(list(CONTROL_BYTES), k=min(16, len(CONTROL_BYTES)))) + PRINTABLE)
    # UTF-8 content
    pieces.append(r.choice(UNICODE_UTF8_SAMPLES))
    # Long-ish ascii
    pieces.append((b"x" * r.randint(50, 300)))
    # Escapable content for sdscatrepr
    pieces.append(b"\"quote\"\\backslash\\\nnew\tTab\rCR\0NULL")
    return pieces

# RESP sets to exercise redisReaderFeed paths

def make_resp_corpus(r: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    items = []
    items.append(resp_simple_string(b"OK"))
    items.append(resp_error(b"ERR something went wrong"))
    items.append(resp_integer(r.randint(-1000, 1000)))
    items.append(resp_bulk(b"hello world"))
    items.append(resp_null_bulk())
    # Array of different types
    arr = [resp_bulk(b"foo"), resp_integer(42), resp_simple_string(b"PONG")]
    items.append(resp_array(arr))
    # Nested array
    nested = resp_array([resp_bulk(b"SET"), resp_bulk(b"k"), resp_bulk(b"v")])
    items.append(resp_array([nested, resp_integer(1)]))
    # PUSH message
    items.append(resp_push([resp_bulk(b"pubsub"), resp_bulk(b"message"), resp_bulk(b"chan"), resp_bulk(b"payload")]))
    return items

# Build a combined buffer that can be used as FUZZ_PARAM_STR input by different stubs.
# Strategy:
# - Randomly pick a scenario among SDS-heavy, RESP-heavy, or mixed.
# - Concatenate several independent valid segments separated by random bytes so that
#   trimming to any prefix (len selection in redisReaderFeed) yields valid prefixes.
# - Ensure overall size <= 4096.

def gen_buffer(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    scenario = r.choice(["sds", "resp", "mixed"]) 
    buf = bytearray()

    def maybe_pad():
        # Random small padding (binary) that is still safe for SDS APIs
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            pad_len = r.randint(0, 16)
            buf.extend(r.randbytes(pad_len))

    if scenario == "resp":
        blocks = make_resp_corpus(r)
        r.shuffle(blocks)
        for b in blocks:
            maybe_pad()
            if len(buf) + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
                break
            buf.extend(b)
        # Add a partial final frame to test incremental feed while still valid prefix
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            tail = resp_bulk(b"partial-frame")
            cut = r.randint(0, min(len(tail), 64))
            if len(buf) + cut <= MAX_TOTAL:
                buf.extend(tail[:cut])

    elif scenario == "sds":
        chunks = sds_interesting_chunks(r)
        r.shuffle(chunks)
        sep_choices = [b",", b"::", b"|", b"\n", b"\t", b" "]
        for ch in chunks:
            maybe_pad()
            if r.random() < 0.4:
                # intersperse chosen separator sequences to help sdssplitlen
                ch = r.choice(sep_choices) + ch + r.choice(sep_choices)
            if len(buf) + len(ch) > MAX_TOTAL:
                break
            buf.extend(ch)
        # Ensure presence of various bytes to exercise sdscatrepr
        extras = [b"\n\r\t", b"\\\"\0"]
        for e in extras:
            if len(buf) + len(e) <= MAX_TOTAL:
                buf.extend(e)

    else:  # mixed
        blocks = []
        blocks.extend(make_resp_corpus(r))
        blocks.extend(sds_interesting_chunks(r))
        r.shuffle(blocks)
        for b in blocks:
            maybe_pad()
            if len(buf) + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
                break
            buf.extend(b)

    # Final adjustment: cap to 2048 bytes to keep inputs modest for per-call truncations
    if len(buf) > 2048:
        buf = buf[:2048]
    # Guarantee non-empty with some probability, but empty is also valid for some calls
    if len(buf) == 0:
        buf.extend(b"\r\n")
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return gen_buffer(r)

import random
